Coppelia. A lighthearted, comedic classical ballet composed by Léo Delibes with choreography by Arthur Saint-Léon. The story is based on E. T. A. Hoffmann's short story "The Sandman" and centers on the romance of two lovers, Franz and Swanhilda, complicated by an eccentric toy-maker named Dr. Coppelius. The doctor has created a life-sized mechanical doll that he places on his balcony, and Franz becomes so infatuated with this doll, believing her to be a real woman, that he forgets about his betrothed Swanhilda. Swanhilda and her friends sneak into the doctor's workshop to investigate, and when they discover that Coppelia is merely a mechanical doll, Swanhilda hides inside the doll's place. When Dr. Coppelius returns and attempts to cast a magic spell that would transfer Franz's life force into the doll, Swanhilda tricks him by pretending the doll has come to life, foiling his plan. The ballet ends with Franz and Swanhilda reconciling and celebrating their marriage with the townspeople. Like The Nutcracker, which is also based on a story by E. T. A. Hoffmann involving toys that come to life, Coppelia plays with the idea of artificial creations blurring the line between object and being.
